description:
There are currently the following types of caching mechanism implementd in the project:
1) caching of tdoc and specification metadata in sqlite database
2) caching of the actual tdoc and specification files in a checkout directory
3) HTTP caching

A new refactoring needs to ensure that the following guidelines are met:
- The checkout dir is currently specified as 'cache_dir / "checkout"' across various places; this must be unified by a helper function from a centralized module.
- HTTP caching must use the same cache_dir path as the database storage and checkout

It might make sense to create a new module on caching and put/move all functionalities in there, even though the caching mechanisms are only losely related?
title: Consolidate all functionalities related to caching

description:
Several related tasks are part of this issue:
1) use rich text console as drain for all loggers (using RichHandler()). 
See: https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/latest/logging.html

2) the CLI already has a "verbose" flag, which should be renamed to "verbosity" and should accept values from logging.NOTSET to logging.CRITICAL *or* any integer number (log level - equivalent to the logging levels). This value should be set for *any* logger instantiated in src/tdoc_crawler ... Default logging level should be: WARNING ... 

3) replace all print() and console.print() that are inteded for logging with logger calls. Exceptions: all console.print commands where console output is explicitly desired, like e.g., everything in #printing.py or the JSON/YAML output 

This change might require to introduce a commonly used factory function like e.g., 

logger = get_logger(name = __name__)
(decorated with functools.cache)

instead of the usual

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

description:
Apart from documentation for coding agents (AGENTS.md, skills, etc.), there are currently these two documentation files are included in the project:

- README.md
- docs/QUICK_REFERENCE.md

In particular QUICK_REFERENCE.md is too long and needs to be refactored into sub-documents. This is the rough plan:

- README.md is seen by the user when opening the git repo page and should contain the most relevant details: briefly describe all main commands of tdoc-crawler with examples.

- a separate document file docs/whatthespec.md: what is it, describe usefulness, but also why it may be "dangerous" to only rely on it - which motivates also the existence of tdoc-crawling via credentials/portal).

- everything related to development setup should be moved into docs/development.md

- a file docs/misc.md with everything else: http caching, checkout directory, etc

- create a kind of "landing page" for documentation as docs/index.md. In there, all other document files are referenced. README.md also refers to docs/index.md for detailed documentation.

- split documentation into docs/crawl.md docs/query.md and docs/utils.md ... each of these documents should describe its purpose first before going into details.

- also have a reference to a new docs/history.md - which simply lists all the entries from docs/history/*.md (latest document should be on top of that list)

- after this refactoring, QUICK_REFERENCE.md should be deleted, as its content is moved into various subdocuments.
title: Refactor documentation

description:
Create a DocumentIdentifier module that applies heuristics to classify documents as 'main' or 'secondary' when multiple docx files exist for a TDoc.

Heuristics to implement:
1. Filename-based: Look for keywords like 'final', 'revised', 'version', 'vX'
2. Size-based: Prefer larger files (likely more complete)
3. Content-based: Analyze document structure (headers, TOC presence)
4. Revision-based: Check for revision relationships via is_revision_of field

Output:
- is_main_document boolean flag in TDocMetadata
- Confidence score for the classification
- Audit log of which heuristic was decisive

Acceptance Criteria:
- Module: src/tdoc_crawler/ai/document_identifier.py
- Unit tests with various document scenarios
- Configurable heuristic weights via config file
- Incremental: Can classify new documents without re-processing existing ones
- Idempotent: Re-running classification on same documents has no effect
title: AI Doc Identifier: Main/secondary classification

description:
Extend the SQLite database schema to support AI processing.

New Tables:
- processing_status: Tracks processing stages (pending, extracting, embedding, summarizing, graphing, completed, failed)
- document_embeddings: Chunk-level embeddings with model versioning, chunk metadata
- document_summaries: Abstracts, technical summaries, key points per document
- graph_nodes: Nodes (documents, concepts, meetings) with temporal validity (valid_from, valid_to)
- graph_edges: Relationships between nodes with weights and temporal context
- document_relationships: Connections between TDocs (revisions, references, discussions)

Fields to add to TDocMetadata:
- processing_status: Current processing state
- date_processed: Timestamp when AI processing completed
- is_main_document: Boolean flag for main vs secondary document classification

Acceptance Criteria:
- All new tables created with proper indexes
- Pydantic models defined for all new tables
- Migrations handled via pydantic-sqlite
- Foreign key relationships established
- Idempotent: Processing same document twice has no effect
- Incremental: New documents add without rebuilding existing data

description:
Create a TemporalGraphBuilder that constructs a knowledge graph with temporal validity for tracking document evolution and relationships.

Features:
- Extract entities and relationships from documents
- Track temporal validity (when concepts were introduced/changed)
- Build graph connecting documents, concepts, meetings, and revisions
- Support temporal queries (e.g., when was feature X discussed)

Technical approach:
- Use LLM for entity/relationship extraction
- NetworkX for graph structure
- Neo4j or custom storage for graph data
- Reference: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti

Output:
- graph_nodes and graph_edges tables populated
- Graph query API for temporal searches
- Visualization support for graph exploration

Acceptance Criteria:
- Module: src/tdoc_crawler/ai/temporal_graph.py
- Temporal validity fields (valid_from, valid_to)
- Relationship types: discusses, revises, references, supersedes
- Unit tests for temporal queries
- Incremental Updates: New documents add nodes/edges without rebuilding entire graph
- Entity Resolution: Link new document entities to existing nodes
- Neo4j or Custom: Use graph DB with incremental update support
title: AI Temporal Graph: Graph-RAG for historical analysis

description:
After successful crawling, downloading and extracting, the following steps are conducted:
- identify "main" document: if number of docx files is >1, apply heuristics for "main" doc. All other files are "secondary" documents.

- extract text/tables/figures/data from docx -> find suitable (AI-based?) tool, save content in Markdown file in each extraction folder (subfolder: .ai)

- processed Markdown files are analyzed via embeddings/LLM to ...generate abstracts/summaries per document upon request

- since the historical order is of high importance in the discussion of TDocs, the embedded data is used to generate a temporal graph-RAG, see e.g., https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.13590 ... or: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti

https://github.com/graphrag/awesome-graphrag
title: AI-based processing of downloaded files

description:
Create an EmbeddingsGenerator that creates vector representations of document chunks for semantic search and retrieval.

Requirements:
- Chunk documents into meaningful segments (paragraphs, sections)
- Generate embeddings using local model (sentence-transformers)
- Store embeddings in database with chunk metadata
- Support for model versioning and updates

Technical approach:
- Model: BAAI/bge or similar domain-adapted model
- Chunk strategy: Section-based with overlap
- Storage: SQLite with vector support or FAISS index

Output:
- document_embeddings table populated with chunk vectors
- Configuration for model selection and chunk parameters
- API for similarity search

Acceptance Criteria:
- Module: src/tdoc_crawler/ai/embeddings.py
- Configurable chunk size and overlap
- Batch processing for efficiency
- Unit tests for embedding quality
- FAISS Index: Use IndexIVFFlat or IndexHNSW for incremental additions
- No Full Rebuild: New embeddings add without rebuilding entire index
- Metadata Tracking: Store document ID, timestamp for each embedding
title: AI Embeddings: Generate document chunk vectors

description:
As a preparation for the "open" command, we need to download crawled tdocs first to a checkout folder (default: next to sqlite database).

The checkout folder should have the same subdirectory structure as the one from 3GPP server.

Tdocs are mainly .zip files, which needs to be extracted after successful download. Always extract the content of each tdoc zip file into a separate folder that is named like the tdoc, e.g., download is: checkout_dir/tsg_sa/sa4/sa4#113 meeting/S4-251234.zip -> content of zip will be found in checkout_dir/tsg_sa/sa4/sa4#113 meeting/S4-251234
title: Download crawled documents to checkout folder
